extracted.intended_audience: investigative journalists, media partners, donors, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational standards and guiding principles for producing large-scale, cross-border investigative journalism focused on transparency, accuracy, collaboration, public-interest impact, and journalist security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / Impact-driven reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: To show people how the world really works through stories that rock the world; forcing positive change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICIJ frames work around exposing wrongdoing so the world can make it right. Stories should punch through the noise, trigger positive change, and serve vital public interest reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency as a core principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency is at the center of everything we do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICIJ emphasizes that access to independently-sourced facts is essential for democracy and a fundamental human right; transparency underpins sourcing, methods, and publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independently-sourced facts / accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Belief that citizens have the right to be better informed; access to independently-sourced facts is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations must rely on independently-sourced facts and rigorous verification. Collaboration and peer scrutiny across cultural and linguistic boundaries are used to improve accuracy and reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative, cross-border reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Persuading the biggest and the smallest media organizations in the world to work together to do the watchdog journalism they used to do alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICIJ organizes large cross-border initiatives, convincing reporters to set aside rivalries to uncover corruption and abuses of power; examples include Offshore Leaks, Panama Papers, Paradise Papers, Pandora Papers and FinCEN Files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and document-driven methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations can involve massive volumes of documents and multi-journalist teams (e.g., combing through more than 25 million documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should be able to handle large, complex data sets and document troves; investigative practice includes document analysis, data forensics, and wide sharing of source material among vetted partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology-driven analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: We build and maintain cutting-edge tools that can pick apart massive and complex data sets, using machine learning and other aspects of artificial intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of advanced tools (ML/AI, bespoke data tools) is central to investigating complex networks, speeding analysis, and enabling discoveries across languages and jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest watchdog journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose corruption, abuses of power and grave harms inflicted on the world’s most vulnerable people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should target matters of vital public interest, push back against misinformation, and aim to inform citizens to hold power to account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of funding and editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ relies entirely on donations; we do not pay media partners. Nor do they pay us for publishing our projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial independence (donor-funded rather than partner-paid) is emphasized to protect editorial independence and avoid commercial pressures from media partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer scrutiny and cross-cultural vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration promotes greater accuracy and depth in our work, through peer scrutiny across cultural, linguistic and journalistic traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer review among partnering reporters to surface errors, contextualize findings, and reduce the risk of being dismissed as biased or erroneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection and support for journalists under threat
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide a layer of security to journalists and media outlets in an era when press freedoms are under attack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer practical protections and support so stories suppressed in one country can appear in another; reassure journalists under threat that they are not isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and global relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Our earth-shaking stories about injustice and abuse of power are made available — and relevant — to billions of people each time we publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reporting is distributed through a wide network of partners, adapted across languages and regions to maximize relevance and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable impact and accountability outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Work has led to public protests, multiple arrests, sweeping legal reform and official inquiries in more than 70 countries, and to resignations of leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate investigations by their tangible outcomes (policy change, legal action, public accountability) as well as recognition (awards, nominations). Impact is a key success metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, capacity building and open sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: We train hundreds of reporters each year, many from poorer countries, and make our technology free for other journalists to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in skills transfer (training, conferences, tips, and free tools) so smaller or resource-poor newsrooms can participate in and benefit from large investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curated, trusted network membership
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ retains a network of trusted journalists, grown by invitation to more than 290 of the best investigative reporters from more than 100 countries and territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a vetted, invitation-based network to protect sources, ensure quality, and coordinate sensitive cross-border projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ’s commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion: acknowledges the value each team member brings and commits to promoting backgrounds and perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively promote DEI to strengthen all dimensions of journalism; integrate diverse voices and perspectives as central to quality reporting.
